subject: Retention signal scrub + escalation plan for expiring accounts
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention signal scrub + escalation plan for expiring accounts

Team —

Quick heads-up: finance asked for a tighter reconciliation of all accounts with renewals inside the next 90 days. I pulled a first-pass snapshot (attached: forecast_snapshot_2026Q4.xlsx) and flagged a short list by retention signal: usage drop > 30% month-over-month, open support tickets > 3 in last 30 days, and any active latency/availability incidents.

Priority asks (can you each own one?):
- Ben: walk your top 8 at-risk deals and confirm stage vs. CRM (we saw a few Commit->Commit-At-Risk flips overnight). Add any missing contract dates.
- Rishi: cover the technical churn signals (KV cache miss spikes, recent incident ties) and prepare a one-slide summary for each account with recommended mitigations.
- Naomi: pull ARR exposure and payment terms for accounts we might need to offer short-term credits or SLA exceptions to retain.

Please update the two tabs in the snapshot by end of day Friday (2026-09-17). If you see an obvious escalation (customer threatening to pause or citing performance), mark it with RED and ping me; I’ll pull in CS and the platform on the call.

I attached the retention playbook (retention_risk_playbook.pdf) with escalation thresholds. Also added BrightByte_SLA_issues.csv — public-facing incidents they referenced in their renewal note earlier this month.

Thanks —
Olga
Director, Renewal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: forecast_snapshot_2026Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet), BrightByte_SLA_issues.csv (csv), retention_risk_playbook.pdf (pdf)

Olga — thanks for the heads-up. I ran the pull for my book and reconciled contract dates for the eight flagged BrightByte rows. Key notes:

- Two contacts (Simon Kaplan, Julia Chen) are showing as "Commit" in CRM but our contract end is 2026-10-29, not 10/15 as the AE had listed. I updated the grid.
- BrightByte has been quiet on adoption for 6 weeks; the product contact hasn’t logged into the console for ~45 days.
- CS escalated an API latency thread on 2026-08-18 (see SLA CSV) — they asked for a status call but didn’t get a scheduled fix until last week.

I left comments in the spreadsheet with recommended next steps per account: patch timeline, short-term credit ask, and an offer for a technical deep-dive with our infra team. I can own Simon’s renewal cadence — I’ll reach out to schedule an exec check-in unless you want to handle the outreach.

Subject: Re: Retention signal scrub + escalation plan for expiring accounts

Ben / Olga — thanks for the outreach and for compiling the snapshot. A few points from our side before any credit/renewal discussion:

- We’ve been hit by intermittent latency and KV misses on our production workload over the last two months. That degraded a customer-facing feature and caused one churn. The incidents listed in your CSV line up with what we saw.
- Procurement (cc’d) needs a firm SLA commitment and a clearer remediation plan before we consider renewing at current terms.
- On usage: we intentionally throttled non-critical generation to control spend while we evaluate model costs; that accounts for the drop in activity.

We’re open to a contract conversation, but it hinges on two things: 1) a delivery timeline for the infra fixes and 2) a temporary amortized pricing option while we validate the infra. Can we get a 30–45 minute technical sync this week with your platform engineer and our SRE?

-Simon
VP Product
BrightByte

Subject: Action plan: BrightByte escalation + forecast adjustments (final)

Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary & next steps so we have a single source of truth for Finance:

1) Stage reconciliation: Ben confirmed CRM vs. contract mismatch. Rishi, please mark "Commit — at risk" in the sheet for BrightByte and add the incident tie to the "risk notes" column. Finance will conservatively count 60% of the current committed ARR toward the quarter until we close the technical sync and agree terms.

2) Escalation: schedule the technical sync with BrightByte SREs. Rishi — can you loop Platform (cc: infra_oncall@redwood.com) and propose two slots: 2026-09-20 10:00AM PT or 2026-09-21 2:00PM PT? Aim for a 30–45 minute remediation + timeline workshop.

3) Mitigations & offers: Naomi, prepare three options for Finance to present if BrightByte requests concessions: a) one-time credit (dollar amount), b) short-term discount tied to throughput, c) SLA-bumped package with an initial trial term. Include revenue impact for each.

4) Communication: Ben, lead the customer-facing outreach (coordinate with me). Use the attached retention playbook benchmarks when discussing credits. I’ll update HubSpot (link below) and mark the forecast as "partial-count" until we have definitive outcomes.

Please confirm ownerships in thread and update the snapshot by 10:00AM PT on 2026-09-19. I’ll brief Finance after you confirm.

Olga
Director, Renewal Ops
Redwood Inference
